region: Hector · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Chateau LaFayette Reneau was founded in 1985 by Dick Reno on the east shore of Seneca Lake, the deepest of the Finger Lakes, and welcomes visitors in a fully restored, century-old barn above the water. Its 110 acres of stony shale slopes catch sun and air flow, conditions the winery credits for both aromatic whites and fuller reds. Since 2013 it has been owned by Gene Pierce, who also owns Glenora and Knapp, with longtime winemaker Tim Miller in the cellar.

Seneca Lake’s eastern shore is known locally as the “banana belt,” where the deep water keeps frosts at bay and gives red grapes the extra weeks they need to ripen. Pinot Noir, the thin-skinned grape of Burgundy, responds to cool climates with perfume rather than power, and the Finger Lakes have become one of the more promising places for it in the eastern United States. The winery makes this wine from vinifera grown along the lake.

The winery’s notes describe cherry, tea leaf and toffee on the nose, with smooth tannins and a moderate finish. It is a light-footed, savory Pinot Noir rather than a big, ripe, heavily oaked one, very much in keeping with its cool lakeside origins, and it sits comfortably beside roast poultry, mushrooms, salmon and dishes from the wood oven.
facts: 110 acres on stony shale, east side of Seneca Lake
